commands.title: List worktrees
commands.description: List the git worktrees of every git folder of the workspace, per folder the current worktree first, then newest commit first. Returns [{repo, path, branch, head, committed, main, current}]: repo is the workspace folder, path the worktree root, branch is empty when detached, head is the short SHA, committed its committer date, and current marks the worktree the folder is switched to.

commands.title: Switch worktree
commands.description: Switch a workspace folder to one of its git worktrees: the editor and new terminals follow it. A folder that is a repo subdirectory maps to the same subdirectory of the worktree.

repo.description: Workspace folder; defaults to the first git folder.

path.description: Worktree root, as listed by git.worktrees.

commands.title: List branches
commands.description: List the branches of every git folder that no worktree has checked out: local branches, then remote-tracking ones without a local branch of the same name, each newest commit first, at most 1500 local and 500 remote-tracking per folder. Returns [{repo, name, remote?}].

commands.title: Switch branch
commands.description: Start switching the current worktree of a folder to a branch: a branch checked out in a worktree switches the folder to that worktree; a local branch runs git switch; a remote-tracking branch switches to its local branch, or creates it with git switch --track. Refuses at once when a git.worktree.switching handler refuses (the editor does while the folder's Neovim has unsaved buffers). Git's refusal (local changes, conflicts) is the operation's error and changes nothing. Returns {id}; poll git.worktree-op-status for the outcome, whose notice carries git's warning about commits left behind a detached HEAD. Once it finishes, a call from the app (not an agent or plugin) also publishes git.outcome {workspace, id, message?, confirm?}.

repo.description: Workspace folder; defaults to the first git folder.

branch.description: Local branch, or remote-tracking branch such as origin/x, as listed by git.branches.

commands.title: New worktree
commands.description: Start creating the worktree <main checkout>/.worktrees/<branch>, then switch to it unless switch is false. Checks out the branch when it exists, else creates it from HEAD of the worktree given as from, default the current worktree. Adds .worktrees/ to .git/info/exclude when the repo does not ignore it. Then copies the files listed in .clubmate/worktree-include and runs .clubmate/setup.sh once the user trusts it; a failing setup.sh removes the worktree and fails the operation. Returns {id}; poll git.worktree-op-status for the outcome. Once it finishes, a call from the app (not an agent or plugin) also publishes git.outcome {workspace, id, message?, confirm?}. Fails at once on an invalid branch, an existing folder, a symlinked .worktrees, or while another git operation runs. With slug the folder is <main checkout>/.worktrees/<slug>. With base "default" a new branch starts from origin/<default> after a fetch; when the fetch fails or that branch isn't there it starts from the local default branch and the operation's note says so. In a folder AFK added that nobody has seen yet it does not fetch and runs none of the repo's hooks or filters during the checkout, so LFS files stay pointers.

repo.description: Workspace folder; defaults to the first git folder.

branch.description: Branch name, also the folder name under .worktrees/ unless slug is given.

slug.description: Folder name under .worktrees/, instead of the branch.

base.description: default: start a new branch from the repo's default branch instead of a worktree's HEAD. from then only picks the worktree the files in worktree-include come from. Ignored when the branch exists.

from.description: Worktree root, as listed by git.worktrees, whose HEAD a new branch starts from; defaults to the current worktree. Ignored when the branch exists.

switch.description: Switch the workspace folder to the new worktree; defaults to true. The path git.worktree-op-status returns is the new worktree either way.

commands.title: Repo facts
commands.description: What a local repo is like before it is connected; the path need not be in the workspace. Uses no network and runs nothing the repo's config names, so behind comes from local refs and fetched is false. Returns {name, path, remote, branch, clean, dirty, behind, ahead, defaultBranch, fetched, brings: {graphs, hooks, instructions, skills}, trusted: {hooks, graphs}}. A path that isn't a git repo fails with invalid_params.

path.description: Absolute path of the repo, a worktree of it or a folder inside it.

commands.title: Repos in a folder
commands.description: The git repos inside a folder that isn't one, for adding them as folders of the workspace; the path need not be in the workspace. Looks two levels down, skipping hidden directories and node_modules, and doesn't look inside a repo it found. The walk stops after 3 s with what it found and partial set. With dates, each repo's last commit is read with git log, which runs nothing the repo's config names, for at most 10 s, and repos come newest commit first, undated ones last by name; without, by name. Returns {path, repo, repos: [{path, name, lastCommit?}], partial}: repo is true, and repos empty, when the path is a git repo or inside one; name is the repo's path below the folder.

dates.description: Read each repo's last commit and sort by it.

commands.title: Clone repo
commands.description: Start cloning a repo with the user's own git credentials, never prompting. Fails at once when into is not empty. Runs outside the workspace's other git operations, for up to 30 minutes. Returns {id}; poll git.worktree-op-status, whose path is the clone. Once it finishes, a call from the app (not an agent or plugin) also publishes git.outcome {workspace, id, message?, confirm?}.

into.description: Absolute folder to clone into, missing or empty.

commands.title: Worktree index
commands.description: Every worktree of every git folder of the workspace, cheap and local: no network and no git status. Same order as git.worktrees. Returns [{repo, path, branch, head, committed, main, current, created?, lastOpened?, madeBy?, merged, remoteGone, locked?, lockWhy?}]: created is when the worktree was made, lastOpened when it last became or stopped being the selection, madeBy the plugin that created it, merged whether the branch's own commits are proven to be in the default branch, remoteGone whether its upstream is gone, locked and lockWhy whether git holds it and why. Answers from a per-folder cache and refreshes it in the background; only a folder not read yet waits for one batch of git.

commands.title: Worktree state
commands.description: What removing these worktrees could lose, read with git status in each, at most 8 at a time. Runs nothing the repo's config names. Returns [{path, dirty, unpushed, ignored, secrets?, orphans, nested, tip, merged, landed, remote, locked?, lockWhy?, error?}] in the order of paths: dirty counts changed and untracked files, ignored the ignored files, secrets the secret-looking ignored files (.env, .env.*, *.pem, *.key, .npmrc, .netrc) not inside an ignored folder, relative to the worktree, unpushed the commits on no remote and not in the local default branch, orphans the commits on no ref, nested the initialised submodules and repos inside it, whose work the other numbers can't see, tip and merged are read now rather than from the index, remote whether a remote-tracking branch of that name exists, landed (only with proof) whether the change is in the default branch by ancestry or an exact git merge-tree, locked and lockWhy whether git holds it, error why a path has no numbers.

paths.description: Worktree roots, as listed by git.worktree-index.

proof.description: Also read landed, which runs more git per path.

commands.title: Worktrees with unpushed commits
commands.description: The linked worktrees whose tip is on no remote and not in the local default branch, as paths. One git rev-list per folder, whatever the number of worktrees, so a sheet can sort hundreds without reading each.

commands.title: Delete a local branch
commands.description: Delete a local branch, for the agents plugin only (Archive, Clean up), with git branch -d rules. Refused when it is the default branch, its tip is not the tip you saw, or a remote branch of that name exists. git branch -d decides; only the exact git merge-tree proof, read right before, goes past it with -D. Never touches a remote branch.

tip.description: The commit you saw on it.

commands.title: Worktree operation status
commands.description: Wait up to 1 s for a worktree create or remove started by git.worktree-new or git.worktree-remove, or a clone started by git.clone. Returns {done, error?, path?, notice?, note?}; path is the new worktree or clone after success, notice a warning worth showing after success, note what git.worktree-new fell back to with base.

id.description: Operation id returned by git.worktree-new, git.worktree-remove or git.clone.

commands.title: Worktree sessions
commands.description: List the workspace's running sessions that started inside the given worktree or have a process whose working directory is inside it now, except sessions owned by plugins that handle git.worktree.removing (the editor's own Neovim). Returns [{id, title}].

commands.title: Worktree remove prompt
commands.description: The question the app asks before removing a linked worktree: refuses the main checkout and the folder's own checkout like git.worktree-remove, and lists the running terminals inside it as git.worktree-sessions does, and the secret-looking ignored files no other worktree holds identically and the commits on no ref that removal would lose. Returns {title, detail?, command, args}; args carry seenSecrets and seenOrphans for what it listed; on approval the app runs command with args.

repo.description: Workspace folder; defaults to the first git folder.

path.description: Worktree root, as listed by git.worktrees.

commands.title: Land a change
commands.description: Land a change as one commit. mode branch (default): squash the branch checked out at path into into (default: the repo's default branch, or your parent session's branch when the finish text names it), commit it with message, then remove that worktree (never the main checkout) and force-delete the branch. mode index: commit what is staged in path, which must have into checked out (sessions working on main itself). In a repo with a land gate (agents.gates), an agent's landing first needs a fresh Fable review of exactly this change: with no verdict it starts one and fails with "review pending: <session>" (end your turn; Clubmate prompts you with the verdict, then call git.land again); changes fails with the findings; after the gate's rounds of changes it waits for the user. A moved target needs a new review. Fails on conflicts (rebase first), on staged changes in the target worktree, or when the target moved meanwhile. Returns {commit, into, source, removed, note}.

path.description: The worktree holding the change: the branch's worktree, or for mode index the worktree with the staged change.

into.description: The branch to land into; default the repo's default branch.

mode.description: branch (default) squashes the worktree's branch; index commits the staged change on the target itself.

commands.title: Remove worktree
commands.description: Start removing a linked git worktree: runs the git.worktree.removing handlers (the editor stops its Neovim; any refusal is the operation's error) and then the git.worktree.vacating ones (agent sessions close), runs .clubmate/teardown.sh once the user trusts it (a failure is only a notice), runs git worktree remove and, when it was current, switches the folder back to its own checkout. Never removes the main checkout, a worktree on the default branch, the checkout of the workspace folder, a locked worktree, a worktree with uncommitted changes, or the branch. Without discard or left it also refuses, before and after the handlers ran, a worktree holding more secret-looking ignored files that no other worktree holds identically, or more commits on no ref, than seenSecrets and seenOrphans. Fails at once while another git operation runs, and in a folder AFK added that nobody has seen yet ("open the title picker to look at it first"). Returns {id}; poll git.worktree-op-status for the outcome. Once it finishes, a call from the app (not an agent or plugin) also publishes git.outcome {workspace, id, message?, confirm?}. When a removing handler refused with unsaved buffers and force was not set, confirm asks to retry with force.

repo.description: Workspace folder; defaults to the first git folder.

path.description: Worktree root, as listed by git.worktrees.

force.description: Passed to git.worktree.removing handlers: the editor stops the worktree's Neovim even with unsaved buffers, discarding their changes.

discard.description: Only the agents plugin, for the user's tick on the Remove folder sheet: remove the worktree with its uncommitted changes. Anyone else gets an error.

left.description: Only the agents plugin: repo has just left the workspace, so it is opened directly. Anyone else gets an error.

seenDirty.description: With discard or left: the changed and untracked files the user saw. More than these, or than seenSecrets or seenOrphans, or any submodule or repo inside it, before teardown keeps the worktree and fails the operation.

seenSecrets.description: The secret-looking ignored files the user saw: with discard or left, secrets on git.worktree-state; without, the ones git.worktree-remove-prompt listed, and only the app may pass it then. Other ignored files don't count.

seenOrphans.description: The commits on no ref the user saw; without discard or left only the app may pass it.
